headline: When the dynamic value is a plain inline style from the start, next-yak folds the static class away and passes the style straight through, landing on `vanilla`'s hand-written inline-style ceiling.

microbench.why: The value is an inline `style` object the component just forwards, so folding removes the static class wrapper and the styled element reduces to a plain tag with an inline style — 0.644 ms/1k, within 6% of `vanilla`'s 0.609 ms/1k hand-written ceiling. Folding still earns its place even here: with it off, `next-yak-9.7-nofold` renders at 0.887 ms/1k (1.4× slower) because the wrapper returns, and the 9.6.0 build sat at 1.30 ms/1k (2.0× slower) before the perf runtime and fold shipped as defaults.

autocannon.why: Under load the folded styled element serves at the inline-style ceiling, a statistical tie with `vanilla` (1242 vs 1213 req/s) — there is no per-request styling work left once the class is static and the value rides inline.

attribution.why: The folded lane's library slice is 0.091 ms and its render (0.681 ms) actually undercuts `vanilla` (0.866 ms), because folding emits tighter markup than the hand-written component. The default-off variants mark the cost of the runtime that folding removes: `next-yak-9.7-nofold` renders in 0.872 ms (lib 0.212), the 9.6.0 build in 1.47 ms (lib 0.481).

hydrate.why: Both lanes hydrate as pure JS with the sheet in the HTML; the folded lane's flatter output edges `vanilla` (45.7 vs 49.2 ms), within their spread.

inp.why: Updating an inline style is the same work for both lanes (~7.5-8.2 ms, inside the interaction spread) — a tie.

mount.why: Cold mount is identical to within noise (62.1 vs 62.5 ms) — one static sheet, an inline style forwarded, nothing to inject.

renderTiming.why: One style recalc for both — parity on the paint path; the styleMs difference (0.103 vs 0.109 ms) is noise.

payload.why: `vanilla` ships the least (5.50 kB gz) with no library at all; the folded styled lane adds only its small runtime (6.51 kB), and folding barely moves it — `next-yak-9.7-nofold` is 6.71 kB.

nsweep.why: At 4000 elements the folded lane scales flat with react-dom, tying `vanilla` (2.71 vs 2.67 ms); the inline value adds no compounding per-element styling cost.

crossCase: `dyn-inline` is the inline-style floor of the dynamic trio. It shows the ceiling that `dyn-fair`'s hand-written workarounds aim for and `dyn-translate`'s naive class-per-value pattern misses: with the value already inline there is no class to regenerate, so next-yak's folded output and `vanilla` converge. Reading the three together, next-yak's own number is near-constant across all of them — the css-var/inline split is compiled in, not paid per case.
